# `curate`

Run one continual-curation tick over every active source: incremental (per-source cursor) ingest, catch-up after downtime, strict idempotency, stale-run recovery, then a conditional ENCRYPTED_GIT publish (LOCAL_ONLY performs no network). This is the single verb the one local-jobs command instance invokes on a schedule; it is also safe to run by hand.

- **group:** `mutation`
- **posture:** `reversible`
- **CLI:** `operator-voice curate`
- **MCP tool:** `curate` (mutation — hidden unless explicitly enabled)

## Arguments

| name | type | required | help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | `str` | optional, default=None — one of ['manual', 'scheduled'] | Who invoked this tick. Defaults to $OVT_CURATE_TRIGGER (set by the local-jobs instance) else 'manual'. |
| `per_source_limit` | `int` | optional, default=None | Max candidates ingested per source this tick (bounded continuation for large catch-up backlogs). Defaults to $OVT_CURATE_PER_SOURCE_LIMIT else unbounded. |

## Examples

```
operator-voice curate
```
```
operator-voice curate --trigger scheduled --per-source-limit 500
```

## Errors

| code | what it means |
|---|---|
| `invalid_arguments` | An argument was missing, had the wrong type, or wasn't one of the allowed choices — nothing changed. |
| `skipped_off` | While the toolkit is off, a curation tick is an inert no-op — never a partial run. |

## Plain-language aliases

- "curate now"
- "run curation"
- "process my sources now"
- "catch up now"
